READ THE MODEL, ASSUMPTIONS & SOURCES+

A transparent simplification.

This is an illustrative heterogeneous, first-order A → B proxy, not a model fitted to a specific reaction. It assumes constant temperature, constant effective surface area, and no reverse reaction.

Changing initial concentration scales initial rate and final product, but does not change the first-order rate constant. Surface area is an explicit linear multiplier for this proxy; it is not a universal rate law.

[B](t) = [A]₀(1 − e−kt)

k = S · A · exp(−Eₐ/RT), with R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. A is calibrated so k = 0.035 s⁻¹ at 25 °C, S = 1, Eₐ = 40 kJ mol⁻¹. The catalyst option uses Eₐ = 35 kJ mol⁻¹ with the same A. These values are illustrative.

Particle motion is a visual aid, not a collision calculation. Animation speed is not a measured reaction rate. The dashed reference always uses the default conditions.

Source: IUPAC · Arrhenius equation
Source: Royal Society of Chemistry · Catalysis

CONCEPT CHECK · NOT AN OFFICIAL EXAM ITEM
In our first-order model, you double the initial concentration while keeping temperature, surface area and catalyst unchanged. What happens?

For this model, rate = k[A]. Which quantity changes when you change only [A]₀?

CONCEPT PREVIEWS, ONE LAB & CURATED CONNECTIONS

    STAY ADD. / V.0.1

    A working beginning.

    This is a frontend design prototype of an independent science and mathematics platform. It is not affiliated with an exam board.

    Available to explore

    • A controllable generative hero, four original concept previews, and an illustrative reaction rates lab.
    • Three curated cross-subject connections, a searchable demo index, and one original practice question with feedback.
    • Model data export, keyboard controls, and reduced-motion support.

    Still to be built and reviewed

    Full courses, exam-board and year mapping, official exam preparation, a problem bank, accounts, progress tracking and a large knowledge graph. Preview content is a draft, not syllabus-verified teaching material.

    All interactions run in your browser. No signup or personal data is required. No simulated enrolments, learner statistics or testimonials are used.

    Explore the working lab

    DESIGNED FOR EXPLORATION

    Make yourself at home.

    Keyboard & motion

    Use Tab to move between controls, Enter or Space to activate buttons, arrow keys to adjust sliders, and Escape to close dialogs. All concept-map nodes are buttons. The ambient animation can be paused below the hero, and follows your device’s reduced-motion preference. Numerical lab results remain available without animation.

    Privacy

    This prototype has no account system, analytics, cookies, tracking pixels or server-side submissions. Preferences and answers last only for the current page session. CSV export creates a file locally. Source links open external websites in a new tab.

    Access information

    Accessibility is a design goal, not a claim of formal certification. The implementation uses semantic sections, native controls, visible focus, labelled visualisations, and text alternatives. No production Core Web Vitals are claimed.
